summary: Order-service quote timeouts are caused by pricing-engine CPU saturation triggered by config change cfg-3120, which at 12:04:00Z ramped feature flag flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100. With Greeks v2 active on all traffic, the GreeksV2Calculator Monte-Carlo (20000 paths) takes 3-9s per quote against a 2000ms deadline budget, driving pricing-engine p99 from ~60ms to ~2600ms, CPU from ~40% to 99%, and error rate from ~0.2% to ~12.5%; order-service then logs ~106 quote timeouts. Traffic is flat (~644 req/s), memory is flat (~49%), and market-data-service is completely healthy (p99 ~40ms, cpu ~45%, error ~0.2%), so the reported market-data-service protobuf serialization deploy dep-6111 is a red herring.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Feature-flag rollout of Greeks v2 to 100% saturated pricing-engine CPU, stalling quotes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-3120 (pricing-engine flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5->100 at 12:04Z) activated the expensive GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo path on all traffic. Each quote runs 20000-path Monte-Carlo taking 3-9s against a 2000ms budget, saturating pricing-engine CPU at ~99% and pushing p99 to ~2600ms; order-service quote calls then exceed their 2500ms timeout and fail.

causal_chain.claim: flag activation enables GreeksV2Calculator on all quotes
Monte-Carlo takes 3-9s vs 2000ms budget -> deadline exceeded errors
CPU saturates ~99%, p99 rises to ~2600ms, error_rate to ~12.5%
order-service quote calls exceed 2500ms and log timeouts

assumptions: The flag value 5->100 means 5% to 100% of traffic uses Greeks v2
GreeksV2 is the new/expensive calculator activated by the flag

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service protobuf serialization change caused quote timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-6111 switched market-data-service quote serialization to protobuf, degrading the pricing-engine -> market-data-service call and causing quote timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: market-data-service p99 (~40ms), cpu (~45%) and error_rate (~0.2%) are flat across the window; the change would have degraded its own telemetry. Onset (12:05Z) is 9 minutes after the 11:56Z deploy and coincides exactly with cfg-3120 at 12:04Z. The fault is CPU-bound compute inside pricing-engine, not a serialization/dependency issue.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Traffic volume outgrew pricing-engine capacity
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A surge in quote requests exceeded pricing-engine provisioned capacity, causing CPU saturation and timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: pricing-engine request_rate is flat (~644 req/s, min 571 to max 741) across the entire window; there is no load increase to explain the CPU jump. CPU rose only after the flag ramp.

facts.statement: pricing-engine p99 rose from ~60ms to ~2600ms starting at the 12:05Z bucket and remained elevated.
pricing-engine CPU rose from ~40% to ~99% at the same 12:05Z bucket.
Config change cfg-3120 ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100 at 12:04:00Z, one minute before onset.
pricing-engine logged GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo runs of 3-9s and 2000ms-budget deadline-exceeded errors from 12:05:21Z.
pricing-engine request_rate was flat (~644 req/s), so no traffic surge occurred.
order-service logged 106 quote-call timeouts against pricing-engine from 12:06:10Z.
market-data-service p99, CPU, and error_rate were flat across the window.
market-data-service deploy dep-6111 (protobuf serialization) occurred at 11:56Z, 9 minutes before onset, with no telemetry impact.
pricing-engine had no code deployments in the window.
pricing-engine memory was flat at ~49%, ruling out memory exhaustion.

assumptions: flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct value is a percentage of traffic, so 5->100 means the GreeksV2 calculator now serves all quotes.
GreeksV2Calculator is the code path gated by the greeks_v2 flag.
The pricing-engine CPU saturation is caused by the Monte-Carlo compute (not an external dependency), consistent with flat request rate and flat downstream telemetry.

timeline.event: Only market-data-service log in window: a single unrelated deprecated-TLS-cipher WARN.
market-data-service deploys v5.2.0 (dep-6111, protobuf serialization); no telemetry impact.
First GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo WARN (6465ms) in pricing-engine; p99 and CPU jump at 12:05Z.
order-service begins logging pricing-engine quote call timeouts.
pricing-engine p99 and CPU still elevated (ongoing, no rollback).

recommended_actions.action: Roll back cfg-3120: set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct back to 5 (or 0).
recommended_actions.rationale: Onset coincides within one minute of the 5->100 ramp; reverting the flag should immediately remove the expensive Monte-Carlo path from most traffic and relieve CPU saturation.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery via pricing-engine p99 (<100ms), CPU (<50%), error_rate (~0.2%) and cessation of order-service quote timeouts after the flag revert.
recommended_actions.rationale: Confirms H1 causal chain and rules out confounders.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back dep-6111; instead verify market-data-service is exonerated before the incident call.
recommended_actions.rationale: market-data-service telemetry is flat; an unnecessary rollback adds risk and would not address the fault.

recommended_actions.action: Re-size Greeks v2: reduce Monte-Carlo path count / add caching or async compute, and ramp the flag gradually with CPU/latency SLO gates.
recommended_actions.rationale: GreeksV2 at 20000 paths takes 3-9s per quote far exceeding the 2000ms budget; the experiment must fit the request budget before full rollout.

recommended_actions.action: Add an automatic guard that trips a feature-flag ramp when pricing-engine CPU exceeds ~85% or p99 exceeds the quote budget.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents a flag ramp (which bypasses code deploy gates) from silently saturating production.

data_gaps: config-audit shard 2/3 did not respond on the first all-services config query (tc-002, partial:true), so other services' config changes in the window cannot be fully excluded; the pricing-engine-scoped query (tc-009) returned cfg-3120 cleanly.
The exact baseline behavior at 5% Greeks v2 traffic and any prior history of the flag is not directly listed; assumed from old_value=5.
No root-cause confirmation from a successful flag rollback yet (the change is still live at 100%), so the causal chain is inferred from timing plus mechanism rather than a verified recovery.
market-data-service internal serialization correctness (protobuf decode on pricing-engine side) was not directly probed; it is inferred safe from flat downstream telemetry.
